Create a transparent production atlas of FIFTEEN fixed cooking-place illustrations for the approved Cook's Pen cookbook game, plus ONE EMPTY cell. Use the attached approved object atlas ONLY as the style reference: scratchy confident irregular black fountain-pen contours, modest crosshatching, mainly warm white interiors, restrained ochre/olive/soft terracotta washes. Hand-observed practical kitchen equipment, not glossy cartoons and not photorealistic. Strong clear silhouettes at 120–170 px displayed width. Each place is an independent small explanatory cookbook vignette, with a very faint short ground stroke to anchor it on paper. No background rectangle.
EXACT FOUR COLUMNS × FOUR ROWS. Generous transparent gutters; every entire object and all handles must stay inside its cell. Row-major:
1. HEARTH FIRE: low stone kitchen hearth with a small visible fire and iron cooking grate; no pots or food.
2. WARM SHELF: single broad wood shelf over a small warm radiator, a folded linen cloth on the shelf; no food or vessels.
3. PROOFING SHELF: wooden two-level proofing rack, cloth draped over one empty round basket; no visible dough, no oven.
4. OVEN: compact brick kitchen oven with open arched doorway, interior rack and warm glow; no loaves.
5. AIR-FED VAT: open wooden fermentation vat with cloth folded at the rim and a small visible air-inlet tube; no labels, distinguish from churn.
6. GRILL: horizontal ridged black iron grate with handles over a low glowing charcoal bed.
7. STOVE: compact solid iron hob with two round burner plates, stout base, no oven arch and no pots.
8. COOKING POT: large tall stainless stockpot with two short handles and lid slightly lifted, mounted on a small burner, faint steam; no food.
9. FRYING PAN: wide shallow cast-iron pan with long handle, on a little hob, contents empty.
10. PASTRY BENCH: broad pale wooden worktable, flour-dusted top and a small bench scraper at its side; no rolling pin, no dough.
11. SAUCEPAN: small deep copper saucepan with long handle on a simple hotplate; distinguish its depth and copper from the shallow frying pan; no food.
12. STEAMER: tall two-tier perforated steel steamer with lid and a little escaping steam on a small burner.
13. CONTROLLED FRUIT LINE: compact professional preserving station: lidded metal processing vessel with gauge and rack for empty glass jars; no filled jars, no words.
14. CONTROLLED STEW LINE: compact professional metal-can seaming machine with lever beside a closed processing vessel and two EMPTY plain tins; clearly different from jar rack.
15. SERVICE HATCH: small open kitchen serving pass, a plain wood frame around an opening in a very small fragment of plaster wall, with a broad counter ledge. Empty. No restaurant scene or plates. Entire vignette stays inside the cell.
16. LEAVE COMPLETELY EMPTY AND TRANSPARENT.
No text, numbers, labels, grid lines, badges, decorative borders, other food, people, extra scenery, or adjacent fragments. Exact 4x4 arrangement, transparent alpha background.
trolley: Generate one isolated EMPTY kitchen serving trolley in the exact Cook's Pen style of the attached approved atlas: searching black pen contours, light irregular crosshatching, restrained warm ochre wood wash, white/transparent open spaces, a little olive-grey metal, handmade observational cookbook drawing. The trolley must have THREE broad usable horizontal shelves and four small caster wheels. Show it almost front-on with only a very slight view of the right side and shelf tops. Width about equal to height (not a tall narrow trolley). Thin unobtrusive rails and legs; large generous open spaces above each shelf. The top shelf must hold a bowl-and-bread plate on the left and a juice jug on the right; the middle shelf must later hold TWO small cakes side by side; the bottom shelf must later hold a tin. Do not draw any of those foods or vessels now. ALL THREE SHELVES COMPLETELY EMPTY. Keep the entire trolley and every wheel/handle visible. Transparent alpha surroundings, no room, no floor rectangle, no labels or numbers or border. This is a production compound base; later transparent food layers will be registered onto the unchanging shelves, so simple nearly frontal geometry matters. Strong black contours must survive display at approximately 190px height. Square image with ample transparent padding.
